item.title: Chilena Codelco reporta alud en mina El Teniente; tres trabajadores afectados
item.description: La cuprífera estatal chilena Codelco dijo el domingo que se registró un alud en su mina El Teniente, afectando a tres trabajadores.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La cuprífera estatal chilena Codelco dijo el domingo que se registró un alud en su mina El Teniente, afectando a tres trabajadores. La compañía explicó que producto de las lluvias caídas en el centro del país se produjo un alud de barro en la operación a rajo abierto del yacimiento. "Inmediatamente se activaron las acciones destinadas a resguardar la integridad de los tres trabajadores que se encontraban en el sector al momento del incidente", dijo en un comunicado. "Uno de ellos fue rescatado y trasladado a un centro asistencial, mientras que los otros dos ya han sido ubicados y se ha iniciado su rescate", agregó sin especificar las condiciones de salud de los operarios. La empresa no detalló el estado de las operaciones tras el incidente.

item.title: Agencia naval británica dice que un petrolero fue embestido por un dron cerca de fondeadero en Omán
item.description: El Servicio de Operaciones de Comercio Marítimo del Reino Unido (UKMTO) informó el lunes de que reclasificó un incidente ocurrido en las proximidades del fondeadero de Sohar, en Omán, como un ataque, tras confirmarse que el petrolero había sido alcanzado por un dron.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Servicio de Operaciones de Comercio Marítimo del Reino Unido (UKMTO) informó el lunes de que reclasificó un incidente ocurrido en las proximidades del fondeadero de Sohar, en Omán, como un ataque, tras confirmarse que el petrolero había sido alcanzado por un dron. Las autoridades locales están colaborando en la evacuación de la tripulación, según la UKMTO, que añadió que, hasta ahora, se desconocen la magnitud de los daños y el impacto medioambiental.

item.title: Al menos 72 mineros artesanales sudaneses mueren en un ataque aéreo, según organización de DDHH
item.description: Al menos 72 mineros artesanales murieron el sábado en un ataque aéreo en el norte de Sudán, informó el domingo la organización de defensa de los derechos humanos Emergency Lawyers, en lo que supone el segundo incidente de este tipo en pocos meses.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Al menos 72 mineros artesanales murieron el sábado en un ataque aéreo en el norte de Sudán, informó el domingo la organización de defensa de los derechos humanos Emergency Lawyers, en lo que supone el segundo incidente de este tipo en pocos meses. Emergency Lawyers atribuyó el ataque a la Fuerza Aérea egipcia, una afirmación que Reuters no pudo verificar de inmediato. El ejército egipcio no hizo comentarios sobre el incidente y el Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. Las imágenes difundidas en las redes sociales y por grupos locales de defensa de derechos humanos, aunque no verificadas por Reuters, muestran decenas de cadáveres esparcidos entre los escombros y otros envueltos en sudarios, así como a mineros que describen un ataque aéreo en la zona. Emergency Lawyers dijo que un ataque transfronterizo de este tipo violaría el derecho internacional. El norte de Sudán ha experimentado una afluencia de mineros artesanales y minas de oro improvisadas, ya que el conflicto en curso en el país ha interrumpido otras fuentes de sustento y el oro se ha convertido en la principal fuente de ingresos para ambas partes beligerantes. Expertos y profesionales del sector afirman que gran parte de ese oro entra de contrabando en Egipto. La guerra entre el ejército de Sudán y las Fuerzas de Apoyo Rápido, de carácter paramilitar, ha provocado cada vez más incidentes con muchas víctimas, sobre todo porque la guerra con drones se está convirtiendo en la principal forma de combate.

item.title: Browns lose rookie WR KC Concepcion (head) on fierce hit
item.description: Cleveland Browns rookie receiver KC Concepcion sustained a head injury midway through the first quarter of Sunday's 17-12 loss to the New York Jets.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Cleveland Browns rookie receiver KC Concepcion sustained a head injury midway through the first quarter of Sunday's 17-12 loss to the New York Jets. Concepcion was injured in the first quarter when Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick crashed into him with a helmet-to-helmet hit. Concepcion remained down on the turf for a few minutes before being helped off the field. Fitzpatrick was penalized for the hit but Browns coach Todd Monken said it wasn't a dirty play on the part of the nine-year veteran. "It's just a bang-bang play," Monken said. "Minkah has been in this league a long time and he's not a dirty player. I've never seen that out of him. It‘s a bang-bang play and unfortunately it happened to our guy. That's part of the league." Concepcion had one catch for 5 yards before exiting. The first-round pick (24th overall) out of Texas A&M has 18 receptions for 149 yards through five games. Browns running back Raheim Sanders (hip) and right tackle Tytus Howard (knee) also sustained injuries during the contest. --Field Level Media

item.title: Texans acquiring Cardinals WR Marvin Harrison Jr., DeMeco Ryans says
item.description: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans told reporters Sunday that the team had acquired wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans told reporters Sunday that the team had acquired wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals. Ryans made the statement to finish his postgame press conference following the Texans' 26-3 road victory over the Tennessee Titans in Nashville. "You guys want to know, huh?" a smiling Ryans said. "Yes, all right, we traded for Marvin Harrison (Jr.). See ya." He ended the press conference and walked away from the podium. Multiple reports Sunday said the Texans are sending a second-round pick and a sixth-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft to the Cardinals in exchange for Harrison and a 2027 seventh-round pick. The teams had not made an official announcement beyond Ryans' declaration. The Texans were rumored during the week to be the team acquiring Harrison after news broke that Arizona was moving on from the fourth overall selection in the 2024 NFL Draft. Harrison was inactive for the Cardinals' home game Sunday against the Detroit Lions, which was in the first quarter when Ryans made his announcement. The 24-year-old Harrison had five catches for 85 yards and one touchdown in Arizona's first four games this season. He caught 62 passes for 885 yards and eight TDs in 17 games (16 starts) as a rookie, and 41 for 608 yards and four TDs over 12 games (10 starts) in 2025. --Field Level Media

item.title: Codelco busca a dos trabajadores desaparecidos tras un deslizamiento en su mayor mina de cobre en Chile
item.description: Las lluvias provocaron un percance en una sección a cielo abierto de El Teniente. Un trabajador fue rescatado y otros dos fueron localizados mientras continuaban las operaciones de rescate.
item.dc:creator: James Attwood
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — La empresa estatal chilena de producción de cobre Codelco se apresura a rescatar a dos trabajadores atrapados en lo que parece ser un deslizamiento de tierra en su gigantesca mina de El Teniente, la misma explotación en la que el año pasado fallecieron seis personas en un accidente y menos de dos semanas después de que se produjera un accidente mortal en otra mina gestionada por la empresa. Las adversas condiciones meteorológicas que afectan al centro de Chile provocaron el percance en una sección a cielo abierto de la mina, según informó Codelco el domingo en un comunicado. Uno de los tres trabajadores que se encontraban en la zona fue rescatado y trasladado a un centro médico, mientras que los otros dos han sido localizados y las operaciones de rescate siguen en marcha. La empresa no ha revelado la identidad de los trabajadores desaparecidos. Ver más: Codelco investiga irregularidades que podrían haber inflado su producción de cobre El accidente se produjo alrededor de las 14:00, hora local, en la zona de Cráter Norte, mientras tres empleados de la empresa contratista AURA realizaban inspecciones, según información preliminar del organismo regulador minero chileno Sernageomin, citada por Radio Cooperativa. El incidente supone el último revés para el mayor país productor de cobre del mundo, que se enfrenta a una caída de la producción, interrupciones operativas y crecientes tensiones laborales, mientras los precios del cobre cotizan cerca de máximos históricos. Estos problemas se producen en un momento de crecientes interrupciones en el suministro, perturbaciones comerciales y una demanda mundial en alza, lo que llevó al cobre a un máximo histórico cercano a los US$15.000 por tonelada el mes pasado. Algunos analistas han pronosticado nuevas subidas en el precio de este metal. Ver más: Codelco dispara sus ganancias un 68% pese a la caída de la producción de cobre El Teniente, la mayor explotación de Codelco, fue escenario de una explosión de rocas en julio de 2025 que causó la muerte de seis trabajadores e interrumpió la producción. A principios de este mes, un trabajador falleció en la mina Radomiro Tomic, perteneciente a la empresa minera con sede en Santiago, poco más de una semana después de que se produjera otro accidente mortal en la explotación de Escondida, del Grupo BHP. Esta última emergencia se produce en un momento en que Codelco, conocida oficialmente como Corporación Nacional del Cobre de Chile, lucha por revertir una caída en la producción, lo que contribuye a un descenso generalizado de la producción chilena de cobre. Las fuertes lluvias, los accidentes y los contratiempos operativos han lastrado las minas del país, mientras que las tensiones laborales se suman a los riesgos de suministro, con trabajadores ya en huelga en Centinela, de Antofagasta Plc, y un conflicto salarial independiente en Escondida, del Grupo BHP. Codelco no facilitó de inmediato detalles sobre el posible impacto en la producción del deslizamiento de tierra del domingo. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

item.title: Amazon in talks to buy AI startup Decart for around $7 billion, WSJ reports
item.description: Amazon is in talks to acquire artificial intelligence startup Decart in a deal that could be valued at around $7 billion, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Amazon (AMZN.O) is in talks to acquire artificial intelligence startup Decart in a deal that could be valued at around $7 billion, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter. Decart's Lucy model, backed by Nvidia (NVDA.O) , can edit live video in real time, according to the company's website. It has also developed Oasis, a model that generates simulated environments to train and test robotics and autonomous-driving systems. Decart was valued at nearly $4 billion in May, the Journal report said, citing PitchBook data. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Decart and Amazon did not respond to requests for comment. A deal could happen soon, if talks do not fall apart or another suitor doesn't emerge, the report said. Last month, Anthropic [USN:L6N450037 TEXT:"decided"] not to pursue an acquisition of Decart after conducting due diligence, Bloomberg News reported. It had [USN:L6N44A04I TEXT:"explored"] the deal in August for potentially $6 billion, Bloomberg reported. Decart raised $300 million in May in a funding round led by Radical Ventures, with Nvidia joining as a new investor.

item.title: Saudi, Iranian foreign ministers discuss regional tensions, state news agency says
item.description: Saudi Arabia's foreign minister spoke with his Iranian counterpart about the recent escalation of the regional conflict and efforts to lower tensions, the Saudi state news agency reported on Sunday, the officials' first publicly reported contact since Iran-aligned Houthis intensified strikes on the kingdom.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabia's foreign minister spoke with his Iranian counterpart about the recent escalation of the regional conflict and efforts to lower tensions, the Saudi state news agency reported on Sunday, the officials' first publicly reported contact since Iran-aligned Houthis intensified strikes on the kingdom. Iran's foreign minister said Tehran is ready to provide any assistance to facilitate dialogue between Saudi Arabia and Yemen, according to a post on the minister's Telegram account. Yemen's Houthis have struck Saudi Arabia several times in the past week, including an [USN:L1N45X01E TEXT:"attack on Riyadh's international airport"] on Saturday that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300. It was the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade.

item.title: Commanders, Giants each squander OT chances in season’s first tie
item.description: Jameis Winston threw two fourth-quarter touchdown passes to force overtime and the New York Giants escaped with a 27-27 tie against the Washington Commanders Sunday in rainy Landover, Md.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jameis Winston threw two fourth-quarter touchdown passes to force overtime and the New York Giants escaped with a 27-27 tie against the Washington Commanders Sunday in rainy Landover, Md. Both teams squandered a chance to win the NFC East showdown late in overtime. The Giants (3-1-1) marched to the Commanders' 24 needing only a field goal to win, but elected to keep driving because kicker Dominic Zvada had missed three of five field-goal attempts - including a 46-yard try in overtime. They gave the ball to Cam Skattebo, who had it stripped and Washington (1-3-1) recovered at its own 23 with 1:55 remaining. Jayden Daniels completed three passes and broke off a 16-yard run to move the Commanders into field-goal range. But on second down at the New York 24 with no timeouts left and 12 seconds to play, Daniels ran up the middle and time expired before Washington could get back to the line and spike the ball. Daniels, who returned after missing two games with a dislocated left elbow and played with a brace, completed 17 of 25 passes for 199 yards. He ran for 103 yards and two touchdowns. Winston was 33 of 54 passing for 326 yards and three scores. Isaiah Likely had 11 catches for 94 yards and two touchdowns while Malik Nabers had 11 grabs for 121 yards and a touchdown. Zvada's 56-yard field goal pulled the Giants within 12-6 with 10:54 left in the third quarter. Washington then went 77 yards in five plays. Daniels capped off the drive with a 38-yard touchdown run with 7:47 left in the third. Winston drove the Giants inside the 10 and, after a pass interference penalty negated a goal-line interception, hit Likely for a 3-yard touchdown to pull New York within 19-13 after three quarters. The Commanders answered with an 81-yard drive that Daniels capped with a 26-yard run. The two-point conversion made it 27-13 with 11:05 to play. New York wasn't done. Winston completed six of eight passes on the ensuing 75-yard drive, which he finished by hitting Likely for a 17-yard score on fourth-and-8 with 7:20 left. The Giants forced a quick punt and, 10 plays later, Winston found a leaping Nabers for a 17-yard touchdown with 1:43 remaining that forged the game's only tie. Daniels completed passes of 11 and 23 yards to Chig Okonkwo on the game's opening drive. On first down at the New York 33, Jacory Croskey-Merritt ran up the middle, cut left and scored. Drew Stevens missed the extra point to leave Washington with a 6-0 lead. Zvada hit from 51 yards with 55 seconds left in the first to make it 6-3. Washington drove inside the 10 early in the second quarter, but after two penalties settled for a Stevens 28-yard field goal and a 9-3 lead. Late in the half, Washington recovered Winston's fumble at the Giants' 27. Stevens hit from 40 yards to make it 12-3 with 1:02 left. --Field Level Media

item.title: Marseille end five-match losing streak and move out of Ligue 1 relegation zone
item.description: Olympique de Marseille won for only the second time in Ligue 1 this season as Amine Harit and Himad Abdelli netted second-half goals in a 2-0 victory at Troyes on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Olympique de Marseille won for only the second time in Ligue 1 this season as Amine Harit and Himad Abdelli netted second-half goals in a 2-0 victory at Troyes on Sunday. The victory lifted Marseille out of the relegation zone and ended a run of five successive defeats in all competitions for the former European champions, who have been hit by financial problems that left them unable to strengthen their squad for the season. Harit, back after a loan spell in Turkey, was unmarked as he tucked away a close-range finish from Emerson’s cross in the 50th minute. Abdelli then scored his first for the club from the penalty spot with the last kick of the game seven minutes into stoppage time. Marseille host Olympiakos in the Europa League on Thursday. The defeat, a fourth successive league loss, dropped promoted Troyes into the bottom two. Earlier on Sunday, Rennes bounced back from a 4-0 defeat at Olympique Lyonnais by thrashing AJ Auxerre 4-1 to move third in Ligue 1, one point behind leaders Monaco. Newly capped France international Esteban Lepaul volleyed Rennes ahead in the 15th minute, but Cameron Archer drew Auxerre level 10 minutes later. The recent arrival from Southampton became the seventh player in Ligue 1 history to score in each of his first four appearances in the competition. Adrien Thomasson's perfectly placed header across goal restored Rennes' lead in the 53rd minute and substitute Boulaye Dia netted twice in stoppage time to take their goal tally for the season to 12 in six games – joint-most in Ligue 1. Nice secured their second consecutive league win as they came from behind to beat RC Strasbourg 2-1. Dario Essugo put the visitors ahead before a Pape Demba Diop own goal and a strike from fullback Jonathan Clauss completed the turnaround.

item.title: BP withdraws from Riyadh energy conference after airport attack
item.description: BP canceled its attendance at the World Petroleum Council Energy Congress in Riyadh, a company spokesperson said on Sunday, after a missile attack on Riyadh's international airport killed 13 people and wounded more than 300.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: BP (BP.L) canceled its attendance at the World Petroleum Council Energy Congress in Riyadh, a company spokesperson said on Sunday, after a missile attack on Riyadh's international airport [USN:L1N45X01E TEXT:"killed 13 people"] and wounded more than 300. The airport has been closed since the attack on Saturday. Saudi authorities reported that people were injured in another attack on the airport on Sunday. The five-day international energy conference went ahead as scheduled on Sunday at a convention centre about 10 km (6.2 miles) from Riyadh airport, the Saudi energy ministry said. BP CEO Meg O'Neill had appeared on previous agendas for the conference. "We made every effort to participate in WPC. Unfortunately, due to travel disruption, we are unable to be there in person. We greatly value our longstanding partnerships across the region," a BP spokesperson said. The Financial Times, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that the CEOs of ExxonMobil (XOM.N) , TotalEnergies (TTEF.PA) and Shell (SHEL.L) had been expected to attend the conference but withdrew. Shell declined to comment, while TotalEnergies and ExxonMobil did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment made outside regular business hours.

item.title: Joe Burrow throws 4 TDs, Bengals hold off Dolphins
item.description: Joe Burrow threw four touchdown passes and Jordan Battle had two interceptions to help the Cincinnati Bengals secure a 31-24 victory over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday afternoon in Miami Gardens, Fla.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Joe Burrow threw four touchdown passes and Jordan Battle had two interceptions to help the Cincinnati Bengals secure a 31-24 victory over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday afternoon in Miami Gardens, Fla. Burrow completed 23 of 32 passes for 190 yards as Cincinnati (3-2) rebounded following back-to-back losses. The Dolphins (0-5) lost their first five games of the season for the first time since starting the 2019 season with seven losses in a row. Ja'Marr Chase, who was in concussion protocol earlier in the week, started and caught six passes for 77 yards. Chase made an acrobatic, leaping catch in the end zone despite tight coverage from Dolphins cornerback Jason Marshall Jr. to snare Burrow's fourth touchdown pass with 39 seconds left in the third quarter, giving the Bengals a 28-10 lead. Ollie Gordon II led the Dolphins in rushing with 88 yards on 18 carries, and a 1-yard touchdown run that tied the game at 7 with 8:02 left in the first quarter. The Dolphins finished with a season-high 331 total yards and ran for 217 yards, which helped them finish with a season-high scoring output. After Chase's touchdown catch, Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis led a 14-play, 80-yard drive that consumed 8:26. Willis capped it with a 3-yard pass to the back of the end zone to rookie Kevin Coleman Jr., who caught his first NFL touchdown. Tight end Greg Dulcich then made a great catch of his own in the back of the end zone for a two-point conversion to cut Cincinnati's lead to 28-18 with 7:13 left in the fourth quarter. The Dolphins forced the Bengals to punt on their ensuing possession. But as Willis looked to scramble up the field on the drive's second play, Jonathan Allen stripped him of the ball and recovered it at Miami's 10 with 2:34 left. That led to a 26-yard field goal by Evan McPherson with 2:09 left. McPherson broke the Bengals' record for consecutive made field goals with his 22nd in a row. Willis completed 15 of 27 passes for 137 yards with two interceptions, and ran for 74 yards on eight attempts. His 1-yard touchdown run with 45 seconds left in the game put Miami within one score. But the Dolphins' ensuing onside kick attempt failed, sealing the win for the Bengals. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jets beat sloppy Browns to snap 3-game skid
item.description: Braelon Allen rushed for 116 yards and the go-ahead touchdown on 24 carries as the New York Jets dampened the hot Cleveland Browns with a 17-12 win on a rainy Sunday afternoon in East Rutherford, N.J.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Braelon Allen rushed for 116 yards and the go-ahead touchdown on 24 carries as the New York Jets dampened the hot Cleveland Browns with a 17-12 win on a rainy Sunday afternoon in East Rutherford, N.J. Trailing 12-10 after leading the majority of the matchup, the Jets (2-3) went up for good when Allen dashed 22 yards for the winning run with 3:01 left. The Jets were set up at the Browns' 23 three plays earlier when Cleveland punter Corey Bojorquez fumbled a snap. Will McDonald IV strip-sacked Deshaun Watson on fourth-and-long inside the final minute to give the Jets their first victory since a Week 1 win at the Tennessee Titans. Geno Smith was 17 of 30 for 182 yards and a touchdown to Garrett Wilson, who had seven receptions for 104 yards. Rookie David Bailey posted three of New York's eight sacks. Cleveland (3-2) suffered from a number of dropped passes that stalled the offense. Watson was 15-for-33 passing for 155 yards and a score to Denzel Boston. Isaiah Bond had three catches for 74 yards. The Browns lost for the first time since a Week 1 setback at the Jacksonville Jaguars. After stuffing the Browns on the first series, the Jets soared away on their initial possession after Bojorquez launched a 67-yarder for a touchback to set up the drive, which ended after eight plays and 80 yards. Wilson ate up 70 of those by snagging three passes from Smith. The former Ohio State star caught the third one over the middle, spun away from Ronnie Hickman at the 20 and raced to paydirt for a 32-yard touchdown and a 7-0 lead at 9:17. Cleveland's Andre Szmyt answered with a 25-yard field goal late in the first, but the 67-yard drive came with a price as rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion took a head shot from safety Minkah Fitzpatrick and was soon ruled out of the game. Szmyt nailed a kick from 41 yards at 10:14, and the Browns remained within 7-6 at halftime. Getting the better end of the field-position game, the Jets tacked on three points when Jason Sanders boomed a 54-yard field goal with 14:37 to play to push it to 10-6. On third-and-10 with just over six minutes left, Boston caught a 29-yard touchdown from Watson, but Szmyt's PAT hit the upright, leaving Cleveland with a 12-10 lead before Allen's game-winning run. --Field Level Media

item.title: Drake Maye (5 total TDs) leads attack as Patriots rout Raiders
item.description: Drake Maye completed 26 of 34 passes for 374 yards and four touchdowns and also rushed for a TD to help the New England Patriots defeat the Las Vegas Raiders 45-17 Sunday in Foxborough, Mass.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Drake Maye completed 26 of 34 passes for 374 yards and four touchdowns and also rushed for a TD to help the New England Patriots defeat the Las Vegas Raiders 45-17 Sunday in Foxborough, Mass. Rhamondre Stevenson added a 5-yard touchdown run for New England, which outgained Las Vegas 536-306. DeMario Douglas had two TD catches for the Patriots. The Raiders (3-2) received a touchdown catch from tight end Brock Bowers (eight receptions, 110 yards) and a TD run from running back Dylan Laube. Maye tossed two touchdown passes in the first half, when New England (3-2) built a 21-7 lead. The Patriots struck first on a 35-yard pass from Maye to Douglas with 11:23 left in the first quarter, but Las Vegas tied the game 7-7 on a 13-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Kirk Cousins to Bowers with 8:19 to go in the period. Stevenson's touchdown run gave New England a 14-7 lead with 1:30 left in the first. Maye's second touchdown pass was an 11-yard completion to tight end Hunter Henry with 24 seconds remaining in the first half. The Patriots extended their lead to 28-7 on a 34-yard scoring pass from Maye to Kyle Williams with 12:58 left in the third quarter. Las Vegas' Matt Gay made a 46-yard field goal with 8:30 left in the third to make it 28-10, but Maye responded with a 3-yard scoring run to push the lead to 35-10 with 3:10 remaining in the period. Andy Borregales' 28-yard field goal 48 seconds into the fourth quarter extended the margin to 38-10. Laube scored his first NFL touchdown on a 2-yard run with 10:49 to play to trim New England's lead to 38-17. The Patriots answered with an 8-yard scoring pass from Maye to Douglas with 6:06 on the clock. New England lost two key offensive players to injuries in the first half. Running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) and left tackle Will Campbell (knee) both went down in the second quarter. Neither returned to the game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jaylen Warren's big plays spark Steelers past Colts
item.description: Jaylen Warren scored on an 80-yard pass and a 50-yard run and Aaron Rodgers threw three touchdown passes for the third straight game to lead the Pittsburgh Steelers to a 34-22 victory over the visiting Indianapolis Colts on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jaylen Warren scored on an 80-yard pass and a 50-yard run and Aaron Rodgers threw three touchdown passes for the third straight game to lead the Pittsburgh Steelers to a 34-22 victory over the visiting Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Pat Freiermuth caught two touchdown passes for Pittsburgh (3-2). Rodgers completed 22 of 31 passes for 235 yards and Warren had 188 yards from scrimmage (101 rushing, 87 receiving) in 21 touches. Spencer Shrader matched the franchise record of five field goals and Tyler Warren rushed for a touchdown for the Colts (2-3), who had a two-game winning streak snapped. Tyler Warren also had a game-high seven receptions for 83 yards. Daniel Jones completed 24 of 44 passes for 267 yards, but Jonathan Taylor gained just 45 yards on 15 rushes. The Steelers lost receivers Roman Wilson (dislocated finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) during the contest to further diminish the position's depth. Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) was placed on injured reserve on Saturday. Shrader kicked a 22-yard field goal with 10:23 left in the third quarter to bring the Colts within 17-16. Five plays later, Jaylen Warren cut through the line at the 50 and saw open field en route to a score that put Pittsburgh up eight with 7:06 left in the third quarter. Shrader tacked on a 40-yard field goal as Indianapolis moved within 24-19 with 2:13 remaining in the third. Early in the fourth quarter, a 20-yard run by Taylor gave the Colts a first down at the Pittsburgh 10-yard line. But Jones threw three straight incompletions and Indianapolis settled for a 28-yard field goal by Shrader. The Steelers then pulled away with Rodgers throwing a 17-yard scoring pass to Freiermuth and Chris Boswell tacking on a 54-yard field goal to make it 34-22 with 3:43 to play. After Shrader opened the scoring with a 57-yard field goal on the Colts' first possession, Pittsburgh scored from its 20 on the next offensive play. Rodgers threw a short pass to Jaylen Warren, who shed a tackler and sped down the right sideline with 8:45 left in the opening quarter. Shrader kicked a 56-yard field goal with 6:55 remaining in the quarter before the Steelers answered. Rodgers capped a 12-play drive with a 1-yard pass to Freiermuth to make it 14-6 with 13:17 left in the half. Indianapolis moved within a point when Tyler Warren, a tight end, lined up in the backfield on fourth down and got into the end zone on second effort for a 1-yard score with 7:43 remaining. Boswell booted a 48-yard field goal with 21 seconds left to give the Steelers a 17-13 halftime lead. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jordan Love airs it out as Packers rout rival Bears
item.description: Jordan Love passed for 367 yards and two touchdowns and MarShawn Lloyd rushed for two scores as the Green Bay Packers routed the visiting Chicago Bears 31-7 on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jordan Love passed for 367 yards and two touchdowns and MarShawn Lloyd rushed for two scores as the Green Bay Packers routed the visiting Chicago Bears 31-7 on Sunday. Xavier McKinney snagged two interceptions while Ty'Ron Hopper added another for Green Bay (3-2), which scored 15 points off five Chicago turnovers while committing no turnovers. Bears quarterback Tyson Bagent was 12-for-21 passing for 87 yards and two picks before being pulled in favor of Case Keenum to begin the fourth quarter. With the Bears driving to cut into their 24-point deficit, Hopper intercepted Keenum at the goal line and returned the ball to the Packers' 19 with 12:49 to play. Green Bay followed with a missed field goal but Chicago (3-2) couldn't respond, turning the ball over on four straight second-half possessions. Rome Odunze and Keenum lost fourth-quarter fumbles. Love completed 25 of 31 passes while showing precision with the deep ball. Watson, who caught both touchdowns, had six catches for 143 yards. Matthew Golden had a 50-yard catch among his six receptions for 123 yards while Tucker Kraft had a 46-yard gain. Green Bay outscored Chicago 17-0 after halftime. A 53-yard TD pass from Love to Watson 1:50 into the third quarter set the tone. D'Andre Swift rushed nine times for 43 yards and a touchdown for Chicago. Luther Burden III had 47 yards on four catches. After forcing a Bears punt on the opening possession, the Packers moved 91 yards on 10 plays to score the game's first touchdown. Love capped the drive with a 42-yard scoring pass to Watson. Love was 5-for-5 for 67 yards on the drive. McKinney intercepted Bagent on Chicago's next series, setting up a short field for the Packers. The result was the same as Green Bay's first possession as Lloyd visited the end zone on a 7-yard run with 14:56 remaining in the second quarter. Chicago trimmed the deficit to 14-7 with 1:56 left before halftime. Swift rushed for a 1-yard touchdown on 4th and goal to punctuate a 16-play, 78-yard drive that took 9:10 off the clock. Bears linebacker T.J. Edwards left the game with a hamstring injury. Trey Smack made a 35-yard field goal for Green Bay, but missed two fourth-quarter attempts and one of his two extra points. The Packers held a pregame moment of silence for former Bears coach Mike Ditka, who also was a Hall of Fame tight end in a career that included six seasons with Chicago. Ditka passed away on Friday at age 86. --Field Level Media

item.title: Vikings remain undefeated, defense dominates Saints
item.description: Kyler Murray went 24 for 30 with one touchdown pass, Aaron Jones rushed for a touchdown and the visiting Minnesota Vikings remained undefeated by beating the New Orleans Saints 23-13 on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kyler Murray went 24 for 30 with one touchdown pass, Aaron Jones rushed for a touchdown and the visiting Minnesota Vikings remained undefeated by beating the New Orleans Saints 23-13 on Sunday afternoon. Murray passed for 229 yards, Jones rushed for 113 and the Vikings (5-0), whose No. 4 defense was allowing an average of 289.3 yards per game, held the Saints (1-4) to 142 yards. Tyler Shough, who entered the game fourth in the league in passing yards, threw for just 96 yards and was intercepted twice for the Saints. New Orleans' Jayden Price fumbled while returning the opening second-half kickoff and Jeshaun Jones recovered for Minnesota at the Saints' 37. Six plays later, Murray threw a 15-yard touchdown pass to Justin Jefferson to give the Vikings a 13-7 lead. On the ensuing possession, Shough was intercepted by Byron Murphy Jr. and Minnesota took over at the New Orleans 37. The Vikings failed to take advantage of the opportunity as Myles Price fumbled a reception, and Jonas Sanker returned it 87 yards for a touchdown, tying the score at 13 at the end of the third quarter. On the second play of the fourth quarter, Jones ran 8 yards for a touchdown to give Minnesota a 20-13 lead. Will Reichard's 34th consecutive made field goal, a 55-yarder, increased the lead to 23-13 midway through the period. The Vikings received the opening kickoff and drove to Reichard's 40-yard field goal, but they lost tight end T.J. Hockenson, their leading receiver, to a concussion during the drive. Minnesota was in position to increase the lead, but Jones fumbled at the New Orleans 3-yard line and Chase Young recovered and returned it to the Saints' 34, leaving the score 3-0 at the end of the first quarter. New Orleans converted two fourth downs during a 15-play drive that ended with Kendre Miller's 2-yard touchdown run for a 7-3 lead midway through the second quarter. Reichard kicked a 54-yard field goal as time expired to get the Vikings within 7-6 at halftime. --Field Level Media

item.title: Texans take down Titans for first win of 2026
item.description: Houston won for the first time this season behind a dominant defensive effort and four Ka'imi Fairbairn field goals to bury the Tennessee Titans 26-3 on Sunday afternoon in Nashville.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Houston won for the first time this season behind a dominant defensive effort and four Ka'imi Fairbairn field goals to bury the Tennessee Titans 26-3 on Sunday afternoon in Nashville. C.J Stroud ran for a 2-yard touchdown in the third quarter and hit Jaylin Noel for a 9-yard score in the fourth to wrap up the Houston victory. The Texans (1-4) made life challenging for Titans quarterback Cam Ward. He was sacked three times by Will Anderson Jr. -- twice on the final drive of the game -- and Danielle Hunter also had a sack for the Texans. Ward was 23-of-36 passing for 170 yards and one interception. Houston started 0-3 last season and made a change in defensive play-caller to get its first victory, which came at the Titans' expense. Prior to this week's game, head coach DeMeco Ryans took over defensive playcalling and Houston again beat Tennessee to find the win column for the first time. Tennessee (0-5) had only 187 total yards of offense and the Texans finished with 329. The Titans have lost seven consecutive games dating back to last season. Stroud, who has six touchdown passes and zero interceptions through five games, completed 26 of 34 passes for 261 yards. Wide receiver Nico Collins had five receptions for 56 yards and Noel had five for 41 yards. The Titans were held scoreless after an opening-drive field goal. The Texans scored second-half touchdowns after Fairbairn ended four consecutive drives with field goals. He had three field goals in the second quarter, including a 53-yarder before the half. Tennessee had only one play over 17 yards, a 23-yard completion from Ward to Calvin Ridley. Woody Marks led the Texans with 62 rushing yards on 16 carries after relieving David Montgomery. Montgomery had five carries for 11 yards, but exited with a groin injury and did not return. --Field Level Media

item.title: Firmas de capital privado exigen mayor participación en ganancias futuras con el ‘super carry’
item.description: Las cláusulas que permiten a los gestores cobrar más del 20% de las ganancias aparecieron en casi un tercio de los nuevos fondos de continuación de un solo activo creados en el primer semestre de 2026 ...
item.dc:creator: Preeti Singh
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — No contentas con el interés preferente estándar, con el que buscan conservar sus inversiones más valiosas, algunas firmas de capital privado ahora exigen un “super carry”. En varios fondos nuevos que estas empresas están creando para conservar determinadas inversiones —conocidos como vehículos de continuación de un único activo—, los responsables de las operaciones exigen una mayor participación en las ganancias futuras. Las cláusulas relativas al super carry —que se refiere a cualquier porcentaje que supere el rango habitual del 12% al 20% correspondiente a la participación en las ganancias— se incluyeron en casi un tercio de los nuevos vehículos de continuación de un único activo creados en el primer semestre de 2026. Esto supone casi el triple del nivel registrado un año antes, según indicó PJT Partners Inc. en un informe. Ver más: ‘Es un mundo de carry’: el comercio de los mercados emergentes registra su racha más larga desde 2008 Cuando Parthenon Capital Partners se propuso ampliar su control sobre Kroll Bond Rating Agency, por ejemplo, la firma de capital riesgo solicitó una mayor participación en las ganancias a cambio de gestionar un nuevo fondo que mantendría la cotizada empresa de la cartera. Aunque varios inversores se mostraron reacios a aceptar las condiciones, HarbourVest Partners acabó aceptando el acuerdo, lo que permitió a Parthenon recaudar más de US$1.700 millones para el vehículo de continuación de un único activo. El crecimiento del super carry en las transacciones secundarias demuestra que, aunque la mayoría de los fondos de capital riesgo tienen dificultades para salir de sus inversiones, las operaciones más codiciadas siguen otorgando ventaja al gestor. Ver más: Goldman Sachs ve el mejor escenario para carry trade en más de dos décadas Las operaciones con super carry podrían suponer un respiro para los gestores estrella que tienen dificultades para obtener siquiera algún tipo de participación en las ganancias de algunos fondos, ya que el aumento de las tasas de interés ha frenado la actividad de negociación. Esto ha llevado a algunos a pasarse a empresas con fondos más rentables, a convertirse en patrocinadores independientes que se centran en una sola operación a la vez o incluso a abandonar el sector por completo. El mero hecho de que los compradores acepten una estructura de super carry no significa que los gestores vayan a poder percibir los pagos más elevados. En primer lugar, deben alcanzar determinados objetivos, y los umbrales varían según la operación. Algunos inversores insistirán en una tasa interna de rentabilidad del 30% o en una rentabilidad sobre el capital invertido de al menos el triple, o en una combinación de ambas. Un negociador señaló que, según las estimaciones internas de su empresa, solo una pequeña parte de dichos acuerdos dará lugar a la activación del super carry. Ver más: Dos monedas de América Latina destacan por su alto carry y menor riesgo, según Goldman Sachs “Los patrocinadores deberían tener un incentivo para seguir maximizando el valor por encima de ciertos niveles dentro del rendimiento de la cartera”, afirmó David Perdue, socio del grupo de asesoramiento estratégico de PJT. En privado, los compradores afirman que aún podrían estar dispuestos a permitir que los gestores de activos se queden con una mayor parte de las ganancias, ya que la competencia por los activos más codiciados es muy reñida. Algunos también ceden debido al historial del gestor del fondo o a su profundo conocimiento sobre un activo subyacente. Aunque algunos posibles inversores se mostraron reacios el año pasado ante la solicitud de Percheron Capital de aplicar un super carry en un fondo de US$1.620 millones para Big Brand Tire & Service, la empresa logró convencer a otros inversores para que aceptaran, entre ellos Blue Owl Capital Inc. ( OWL ), Iconiq y Warburg Pincus. “En general, apoyamos estructuras que alinean los intereses de los promotores con los de los inversores, pagando más a los promotores únicamente cuando los inversores obtienen mayores ganancias”, afirmó un portavoz de Blue Owl en un comunicado enviado por correo electrónico, aunque se negó a comentar sobre una operación concreta. El fondo Sage de Leonard Green & Partners, que respalda fondos de continuación de un único activo, aceptó una estructura de super carry para la operación de Falfurrias Management Partners sobre Crosslake, una empresa de asesoramiento tecnológico. Ver más: ¿Caras o baratas? Expertos de mercado explican cómo ven las acciones de IA Accel-KKR, que ya aplica el super carry en sus fondos principales, convenció a los compradores de sus fondos de continuación para que aceptaran también una prima, aunque con un umbral de rentabilidad más elevado, según fuentes familiarizadas con el asunto. No todos los gestores de fondos pueden convencer a los inversores de que les paguen una super carry . Lightspeed Venture Partners, que busca recaudar US$600 millones para un fondo de continuación multiactivos, propuso una super carry del 25% para la operación, pero el comprador principal, Coller EQT, rechazó la propuesta, según fuentes familiarizadas con las negociaciones. Los representantes de las empresas se negaron a hacer comentarios o no respondieron a los mensajes en los que se les solicitaban comentarios. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

item.title: Pelicans being cautious with G Dejounte Murray’s toe contusion
item.description: New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray is still dealing with a toe contusion and did not participate in Saturday's practice.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray is still dealing with a toe contusion and did not participate in Saturday's practice. The former All-Star played in the Pelicans' first preseason game, recording six points, six assists and four rebounds against the Oklahoma City Thunder. However, he sat out of their matchup against the Miami Heat on Thursday. "We are going to continue to be precautionary about it," Pelicans coach Jamahl Mosley told reporters on Saturday. "We're just going to keep evaluating him and how he responds to the treatment we're giving him. So right now, to try to gauge whether it is playing or not playing, we're 10 days into training camp. So, I'll evaluate that once we start to get into regular-season games." Murray has missed significant time due to injuries since joining the Pelicans ahead of the 2024-25 season, appearing in 45 total games over the last two seasons. During that span, he's averaged 17.2 points, 7.0 assists, 6.1 rebounds and 1.9 steals. --Field Level Media

item.title: Lula y Bolsonaro buscan votos y apoyo político en São Paulo
item.description: Los candidatos reunieron el domingo a sus seguidores y a políticos en São Paulo, la capital del estado más grande del país, antes de la segunda vuelta del 25 de octubre, en la recta final de unas polarizadas elecciones presidenciales.
item.dc:creator: Isabel Teles, Luciana Novaes Magalhaes
item.content:encoded: Los candidatos reunieron el domingo a sus seguidores y a políticos en São Paulo, la capital del estado más grande del país, antes de la segunda vuelta del 25 de octubre, en la recta final de unas polarizadas elecciones presidenciales. El senador conservador Flavio Bolsonaro, que lideró la primera vuelta el 4 de octubre con un 47% de los votos, se reunió con el gobernador reelegido de São Paulo, Tarcisio de Freitas. Aprovechando el impulso inicial tras las elecciones, Bolsonaro centró sus esfuerzos de campaña del domingo en conseguir apoyo político en reuniones con alcaldes y concejales. "Quiero estar muy cerca de cada uno de ustedes, alcaldes. Así es como vamos a construir un Brasil verdaderamente mejor, porque los recursos federales llegarán a la base", dijo el hijo del expresidente Jair Bolsonaro, prometiendo que los municipios recibirían más financiación para combatir la delincuencia si resultaba elegido. Mientras tanto, el presidente en funciones, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, que se situó dos puntos porcentuales por detrás en el recuento inicial, encabezó un gran mitin en la Avenida Paulista. En declaraciones a periodistas antes de subir al escenario, el líder de izquierdas prometió redoblar los esfuerzos en materia de seguridad pública, una de las principales preocupaciones de los votantes. "Para la clase trabajadora, para la comunidad, para el territorio, protección; para los delincuentes, la cárcel", dijo Lula, quien añadió que, si resulta reelegido, quiere reformar el enfoque nacional frente a la delincuencia con la participación directa del Gobierno federal. Desde lo alto de un camión con megafonía, el presidente instó a los votantes jóvenes —que constituían una gran parte de la multitud— a acudir a las urnas, al tiempo que hacía un llamamiento a los ciudadanos de más edad, para quienes el voto es opcional a partir de los 70 años. Carlos Teobaldo da Silva, de 79 años, empleado jubilado de Petrobras que ascendió desde albañil hasta supervisor de mantenimiento, acudió al mitin con el uniforme naranja de la empresa. Da Silva contó que se sentía en la obligación de votar por Lula, a pesar de que a su edad el voto es opcional. "Creo en un cambio de rumbo y seguiré luchando por la reelección de Lula y sus proyectos", dijo Silva.

item.title: UK PM Burnham to release details of dealings with Manchester City
item.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he would publish details of his dealings with Manchester City, after opposition politicians criticised his response to a ruling that found the club guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he would publish details of his dealings with Manchester City, after opposition politicians criticised his response to a ruling that found the club guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules. City appealed the independent commission's ruling earlier this month as the club [USN:L6N45K0U6 TEXT:"seeks to overturn"] the verdict and avoid potentially severe sanctions. The Premier League said City had used "sham" commercial contracts as part of schemes to inflate revenue and understate costs by more than £900 million ($1.19 billion). City have denied wrongdoing throughout the case and said the commission's opinion contains "clear material errors". The [USN:L8N45O1GS TEXT:"UK's Liberal Democrats"] earlier this month urged Burnham to disclose any meetings he had held with Manchester City's owners, Abu Dhabi representatives or related entities. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has also called on the British government to release details of meetings between Burnham and senior City figures. "I've been asked by the leader of the opposition to publish details of my meetings, which I'm happy to do and I'm going to," Burnham said in "The Rest is Politics" podcast, due to be released on Monday. "I will quite clearly put out there everything that I have done working with them in my previous role as Mayor of Greater Manchester." Burnham, who served as the mayor from May 2017 to June 2026, said his contacts with the club were not recent. "None of it is recent, actually, in terms of the meetings I had. I only had one significant meeting, actually, and that was in 2021," he said. Burnham expressed concern in September that City's owners could sell the club after the guilty verdict, saying they had been "a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester" and "in turning the club into a global force". ($1 = 0.7557 pounds)

item.title: Irán considera insuficiente respuesta de EEUU a su propuesta para reabrir Ormuz: medios estatales
item.description: El secretario del Consejo Supremo de Seguridad Nacional de Irán, Mohsen Rezaei, dijo que la respuesta de Estados Unidos a las siete condiciones planteadas por Irán para reabrir el estratégico estrecho de Ormuz era "insuficiente", informaron el domingo medios de comunicación estatales iraníes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El secretario del Consejo Supremo de Seguridad Nacional de Irán, Mohsen Rezaei, dijo que la respuesta de Estados Unidos a las siete condiciones planteadas por Irán para reabrir el estratégico estrecho de Ormuz era "insuficiente", informaron el domingo medios de comunicación estatales iraníes. Washington debe despejar las cuestiones que siguen sin estar claras para Teherán, añadió el responsable de seguridad iraní.

item.title: Who’s singing now? Maresca wants Man City to drown out noise
item.description: Manchester City have spent the last two weeks surrounded by a lot of noise. On Sunday at Anfield, City boss Enzo Maresca told his players the best way to drown it out was by making even more of their own.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Manchester City have spent the last two weeks surrounded by a lot of noise. On Sunday at Anfield, City boss Enzo Maresca told his players the best way to drown it out was by making even more of their own. City did just that with a defiant 3-0 victory over Liverpool that preserved their perfect Premier League start for a three-point lead atop the table. In their first game since an independent commission found the club guilty of 114 breaches of the league's financial rules, City were met by deafening boos and angry chants but left Anfield with their own supporters providing the soundtrack. It was exactly the response Maresca had demanded from his players. "We need to learn how to deal with the outside noise because of the situation, and the noise will be always there," Maresca said. "But at the same time, we need to try to make our noise, and that is win games, like we have done today, because at the end of the game, our fans, they were singing, so the noise was from us, not from Liverpool." The Italian knows the hostility is unlikely to disappear, with Sunday's reception at Anfield a sign of what awaits City on their travels as they await the outcome of their appeal against the financial-rule verdict. "I think (at) all the away games there's going to be noise," said Maresca, who wrapped his coaching staff in a huge hug at the final whistle before he and the players made a beeline for the away fans section to celebrate. "That's why I'm saying that we need to learn how to deal with noise, but at the same time we need to make our noise. Our noise is: who is singing at the end? This has to be our target in this moment." City's response on the pitch matched one of defiance off it. The club's chief executive Ferran Soriano and director of football Hugo Viana travelled with the team to Anfield, a show of unity ahead of one of the most daunting fixtures on the calendar even in less turbulent times. "We were all together," Maresca said. "I think for the importance of the game, Liverpool away, Anfield away, it's a good idea from the club to be all together, the togetherness that in this moment we need." The manager said the players had found the last fortnight difficult, but praised the way they had shut out the turmoil and concentrated on football. City struggled in the first half but took full control after Liverpool's Ryan Gravenberch was shown a red card in the 62nd minute, with Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki scoring. "It was not easy for the players after the last two weeks," he said. "I think they dealt with all the situation very well. "In this moment, all the organisation needs this kind of win like today," he added. "It's good for us coaching staff. It's good for the players. It's good for the fans. It's good for the organisation." City have denied all wrongdoing and have appealed the decision. As for what comes next in their legal battle, Maresca was just as direct. "I'm here to try to prepare for the games and win games," he said. "I've said many times: hopefully, I can speak about this situation when we win the appeal." For now, City's answer to the hostility: not to quieten the racket, but to drown it out with the sounds of victory.

item.title: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro fazem campanha em São Paulo a duas semanas da eleição
item.description: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), candidato à reeleição, e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) reuniram apoiadores e políticos neste domingo em São Paulo, a duas semanas do segundo turno das eleições, marcado para 25 de outubro.
item.dc:creator: Isabel Teles, Luciana Novaes Magalhaes
item.content:encoded: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), candidato à reeleição, e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) reuniram apoiadores e políticos neste domingo em São Paulo, a duas semanas do segundo turno das eleições, marcado para 25 de outubro. Flávio Bolsonaro, que liderou o primeiro turno em 4 de outubro com 47% dos votos, se reuniu com o governador reeleito de São Paulo, Tarcísio de Freitas. Aproveitando o ímpeto após o primeiro turno, o senador concentrou seus esforços de campanha no domingo em garantir apoio político por meio de reuniões com prefeitos e vereadores. “Eu sou um municipalista por convicção; eu quero estar muito próximo de cada um de vocês, prefeitos. É assim que a gente vai conseguir construir um Brasil melhor de verdade porque os recursos federais vão chegar na ponta da linha”, disse o filho mais velho do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, prometendo que os municípios receberão mais verbas para combater o crime caso ele seja eleito. Já o presidente Lula, que ficou cerca de dois pontos percentuais atrás na contagem inicial, foi a atração de um grande comício na Avenida Paulista. Ao falar com repórteres antes de subir ao palco, Lula prometeu redobrar os esforços em segurança pública, uma das principais preocupações dos eleitores. “Para o povo trabalhador, para a comunidade, para o território, proteção para os bandidos, prisão”, disse Lula, acrescentando que, se reeleito, pretende reformular a abordagem nacional ao crime com o envolvimento direto do governo federal. Do alto de um caminhão de som, o presidente fez um apelo aos jovens eleitores, que constituíam grande parte da multidão, a comparecerem às urnas, ao mesmo tempo em que reforçou esse pedido aos cidadãos mais idosos, para quem o voto é opcional a partir dos 70 anos. Carlos Teobaldo da Silva, de 79 anos, aposentado da Petrobras, que subiu na carreira de pedreiro a supervisor de manutenção, vestiu seu uniforme laranja da empresa para o comício. Ele disse que se sente compelido a votar em Lula, mesmo que o voto seja opcional na sua idade. “Estou crente na virada, vou continuar lutando pela reeleição e pelos projetos do Lula”, afirmou.

item.title: Ukraine-Des attaques russes font six morts et 20 blessés
item.description: Des attaques russes ont fait six morts dans deux villes ukrainiennes dimanche, notamment lors d'un bombardement visant une épicerie à Kharkiv, la deuxième plus grande ville du pays.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Des attaques russes ont fait six morts dans deux villes ukrainiennes dimanche, notamment lors d'un bombardement visant une épicerie à Kharkiv, la deuxième plus grande ville du pays. Le gouverneur de la région de Kharkiv, Oleh Syniehubov, a fait état sur Telegram de trois morts et de 20 blessés, précisant que des enfants figuraient parmi ces derniers. Des photos publiées en ligne montraient des équipes de secours s'affairant autour de bâtiments gravement endommagés et de véhicules calcinés. Les autorités ukrainiennes ont également indiqué qu'une autre frappe russe avait fait trois morts dans l'ouest du pays. Ces annonces interviennent après que le président américain Donald Trump [USN:L8N45X03P TEXT:"a fait état"] dimanche d'un accord de cessez-le-feu entre l'Ukraine et la Russie portant sur les infrastructures énergétiques et de son entrée en vigueur immédiate.

item.title: At least 72 Sudanese artisanal miners killed in strike, rights monitor says
item.description: At least 72 artisanal miners were killed in an airstrike in northern Sudan on Saturday, rights monitor Emergency Lawyers said on Sunday, in the second such incident in several months.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: At least 72 artisanal miners were killed in an airstrike in northern Sudan on Saturday, rights monitor Emergency Lawyers said on Sunday, in the second such incident in several months. Emergency Lawyers blamed the Egyptian air force for the strike, a claim Reuters could not immediately verify. The Egyptian military did not comment on the incident and Egypt's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Images shared on social media and by local rights groups but not verified by Reuters show dozens of bodies strewn in rubble and others wrapped in funeral shrouds, and miners describing an airstrike on the area. Emergency Lawyers said such a cross-border attack would violate international law. Northern Sudan has seen an influx of artisanal miners and makeshift gold mines as the country's ongoing conflict disrupted other sources of livelihoods and gold became the key cash source for both warring parties. Experts and those in the sector say much of that gold is smuggled into Egypt. The war between Sudan's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces has seen an increased frequency of mass-casualty events, particularly as drone warfare becomes the primary mode of fighting. On Friday, some 31 people were killed in a drone strike on a displacement camp in an army-controlled area of Sudan's Blue Nile state, one of the war's frontlines, according to the United Nations.

item.title: Kings C Maxime Raynaud (knee) to be re-evaluated in 2 weeks
item.description: Sacramento Kings center Maxime Raynaud suffered a right patellar subluxation in his right knee and will be re-evaluated in approximately two weeks, the team announced Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Sacramento Kings center Maxime Raynaud suffered a right patellar subluxation in his right knee and will be re-evaluated in approximately two weeks, the team announced Sunday afternoon. Raynaud sustained the injury in the second quarter of a preseason game against the Golden State Warriors on Saturday night. Last season, he was a second-team All-Rookie selection, averaging 12.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 1.4 blocks in 74 games (56 starts). He shot 57.1% from the field and 32.4% from three. After the All-Star break, the 23-year-old really broke out, raising his averages to 17.3 points and 9.2 rebounds. Domantas Sabonis is locked in as the Kings' starting center. With Raynaud sidelined, they should rely more on Precious Achiuwa and Dylan Cardwell in reserve minutes. --Field Level Media

item.title: Russian attacks kill six people in two Ukrainian cities
item.description: Russian attacks killed six people in two Ukrainian cities on Sunday, including a strike on a grocery store in Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city, where three people died and 20 were injured, officials said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russian attacks killed six people in two Ukrainian cities on Sunday, including a strike on a grocery store in Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city, where three people died and 20 were injured, officials said. Regional Governor Oleh Syniehubov, writing on Telegram, said two children were among the injured. Pictures posted online showed emergency crews moving around badly damaged buildings and burned-out vehicles. In a separate attack in western Ukraine, officials said a Russian strike killed three people.

item.title: Rallying in Sao Paulo, presidential candidates seek votes and political support
item.description: With Brazil's polarized presidential election entering its final stretch, candidates rallied supporters and politicians on Sunday in Sao Paulo, the nation's largest state capital, ahead of the October 25 runoff.
item.dc:creator: Isabel Teles, Luciana Novaes Magalhaes
item.content:encoded: With Brazil's polarized presidential election entering its final stretch, candidates rallied supporters and politicians on Sunday in Sao Paulo, the nation's largest state capital, ahead of the October 25 runoff. Conservative Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, who led the first round on October 4 with 47% of the vote, met with reelected Sao Paulo Governor Tarcisio de Freitas. Building on his early post-election momentum, Bolsonaro focused his Sunday campaign efforts on securing political backing by meeting with mayors and city councilors. "I want to be very close to each one of you, mayors. This is how we are going to build a truly better Brazil, because federal resources will reach the ground level," the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro said, promising that municipalities would receive more funding to combat crime if he is elected. Meanwhile, incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who trailed by two percentage points in the initial vote, headlined a major rally on Avenida Paulista. Speaking to reporters before taking the stage, the leftist leader promised to redouble efforts on public safety, a top worry for voters. "For the working people, for the community, for the territory, protection; for criminals, prison," Lula said, adding that if reelected, he wants to overhaul the national approach to crime with direct federal government involvement. From atop a sound truck, the president urged young voters, who made up a large portion of the crowd, to turn out, while also appealing to older citizens, for whom voting is optional after age 70. Retired Petrobras employee Carlos Teobaldo da Silva, 79, who rose through the ranks from bricklayer to maintenance supervisor, wore his orange company uniform to the rally. He said he felt compelled to vote for Lula, even though voting is optional at his age. "I believe in a turnaround, and I will keep fighting for Lula's reelection and his projects," Silva said.

item.title: Nepal pede que moradores deixem região após enchente causada por deslizamento; 5 pessoas estão desaparecidas
item.description: Autoridades nepalesas instaram os moradores, neste domingo, a se deslocarem para locais mais seguros depois que uma enchente em um rio na região central do país arrasou várias casas e infraestruturas, mas não houve relatos de vítimas.
item.dc:creator: Gopal Sharma
item.content:encoded: Autoridades nepalesas instaram os moradores, neste domingo, a se deslocarem para locais mais seguros depois que uma enchente em um rio na região central do país arrasou várias casas e infraestruturas, mas não houve relatos de vítimas. Duas mulheres e três homens estavam desaparecidos, informou a autoridade nacional de desastres. O Exército disse que outras 49 pessoas, incluindo um estrangeiro, foram resgatadas. A nacionalidade da pessoa não foi divulgada. Um deslizamento de terra na vila de Chumnubri, no distrito de Gorkha, a cerca de 100 km a oeste de Catmandu, bloqueou o rio Budhi Gandaki, causando inundações, informaram as autoridades. O Budhi Gandaki é um afluente do rio Trishuli, a jusante de outro afluente onde o colapso de uma geleira causou uma enchente catastrófica em agosto, que matou 1.457 pessoas, com milhares ainda desaparecidas. “Pedimos aos moradores que vivem ao longo das margens do rio, a jusante, que deixem a área e se mantenham em segurança”, disse Dharmendra Kumar Mishra, autoridade de alto escalão do distrito de Gorkha. A enchente arrastou cerca de uma dúzia de casas e danificou um acampamento de um projeto hidrelétrico, levando consigo parte do equipamento de construção, informou a Autoridade Nacional de Redução e Gestão de Riscos de Desastres.

item.title: Real Betis beat Osasuna to go third in LaLiga
item.description: Real Betis playmaker Isco netted a goal in each half as his side breezed to a 5-2 home win over Osasuna on Sunday that lifts them to third place in LaLiga, five points behind leaders Barcelona and one ahead of Real Madrid.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Real Betis playmaker Isco netted a goal in each half as his side breezed to a 5-2 home win over Osasuna on Sunday that lifts them to third place in LaLiga, five points behind leaders Barcelona and one ahead of Real Madrid. Isco fired home from the penalty spot in the 10th minute to open the scoring, and Abde Ezzalzouli added a second before the break after Betis won the ball high up the pitch and countered quickly. Betis looked to be set for a comfortable afternoon when Diego Llorente added a third three minutes after halftime, but two quick goals for the visitors from Ante Budimir and Raul Garcia reduced the deficit to 3-2 in the 56th minute. However, Isco eased their nerves again when he snapped up a loose ball in the box and rifled it home, and Jose Antonio Morante came off the bench in the 90th minute to make his LaLiga debut before scoring deep into stoppage time to leave Betis on 19 points after eight games. Earlier on Sunday, Real Sociedad held off a spirited comeback from Deportivo La Coruna to emerge with a 3-2 win at home, while struggling Elche grabbed a much-needed point by holding visitors Celta Vigo to a scoreless draw. In the evening's late kick-off, second-from-bottom Valencia came back from a goal down to grab a point in a 2-2 draw away to Racing Santander. Dani Raba got the visitors off to a great start when he latched on to a long ball and kept his cool to cut inside two defenders and fire home in the second minute to give his side a 1-0 lead, but Yassir Zabiri levelled in the 32nd minute with a finish low into the bottom corner. Ivan Martin gave the home side the lead two minutes into the second half but 18-year-old substitute David Otorbi grabbed a point for Valencia with a well-taken finish in the 65th minute. Valencia are 19th on five points after eight games, one ahead of bottom side Malaga and behind Levante on goal difference. Elche are one point above the drop zone and ahead of Valencia, while 16th-placed Osasuna were among a cluster of eight teams locked on eight points.

item.title: Pats RB TreVeyon Henderson, LT Will Campbell questionable to return vs. Raiders
item.description: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) and starting left tackle Will Campbell (knee) were both injured during the first half of Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders and are questionable to return.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) and starting left tackle Will Campbell (knee) were both injured during the first half of Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders and are questionable to return. Henderson gained 22 yards on four carries and had one catch for 16 yards before he left the game. His injury will likely result in more playing time for Rhamondre Stevenson, who scored on a 5-yard run in the first quarter and has 57 rushing yards at halftime with New England leading 21-7. Caleb Lomu, New England's first-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, replaced Campbell at left tackle. --Field Level Media

item.title: Georgia back atop AP Poll for first time since 2024
item.description: Georgia is the No. 1 team in Sunday's updated Associated Press poll, replacing Texas, which fell six spots to No. 7 after its 27-24 loss to rival Oklahoma on Saturday in Dallas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Georgia is the No. 1 team in Sunday's updated Associated Press poll, replacing Texas, which fell six spots to No. 7 after its 27-24 loss to rival Oklahoma on Saturday in Dallas. The Bulldogs (6-0, 4-0 Southeastern Conference) cemented their place as SEC front-runners with their 20-17 win at Alabama on Saturday. The Crimson Tide held firm at No. 6 despite the loss. Georgia, which won consecutive national championships in 2021 and 2022, is the No. 1 team in the AP poll for the first time since Sept. 8, 2024, after spending the previous five weeks at No. 2. Notre Dame, Miami (Fla.) and Ohio State each moved up a spot thanks to Texas' plummet, while Indiana improved two spots to round out the new top five. LSU is the only team to fall out of this week's top 10, dropping 12 spots to No. 22 after its 35-34 overtime loss at Kentucky. Texas Tech moved up one spot to No. 10, taking the Tigers' place. Kentucky, conversely, took the biggest leap in this week's poll, jumping up 11 spots from first team out to No. 15. UCLA's 17-15 win at Oregon also proved significant in this week's rankings, with the Bruins moving up nine spots to No. 12 while the Ducks, who were the preseason No. 2 team, fell out of this week's poll, their first time outside the Top 25 since 2022. Along with Kentucky, Wake Forest and Northwestern are additions to this week's poll at Nos. 21 and 25, respectively. It's the first time Wake Forest has been ranked since 2022 and Northwestern's first ranking since 2020. Florida, ranked eighth two weeks ago, fell out of this week's poll after its second consecutive lopsided loss, this one 38-19 at home against South Carolina. Pitt, 25th last week, also fell out of the poll after its 21-17 home loss to North Carolina. AP Top 25 1. Georgia (6-0) 2. Notre Dame (6-0) 3. Miami (Fla.) (5-0) 4. Ohio State (5-1) 5. Indiana (6-0) 6. Alabama (5-1) 7. Texas (4-1) 8. BYU (5-0) 9. Ole Miss (4-1) 10. Texas Tech (5-0) 11. Utah (5-0) 12. UCLA (5-0) 13. Missouri (5-1) 14. Tennessee (5-1) 15. Kentucky (5-1) 16. Mississippi State (4-1) 17. Iowa (5-1) 18. Oklahoma State (4-1) 19. USC (6-1) 20. Houston (5-1) 21. Wake Forest (5-1) 22. LSU (4-2) 23. Boise State (5-1) 24. SMU (4-1) 25. Northwestern (4-1) --Field Level Media

item.title: Dodgers add LHP Justin Wrobleski to NLCS roster
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers added left-hander Justin Wrobleski to their roster for the National League Championship Series on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Los Angeles Dodgers added left-hander Justin Wrobleski to their roster for the National League Championship Series on Sunday. The 26-year-old had a 12-5 record, 3.66 ERA and 1.143 WHIP in 28 games (22 starts) and earned his first All-Star selection this season. He shifted to the bullpen in September. Los Angeles will rely on Wrobleski to provide depth in the best-of-seven series against the Milwaukee Brewers. Game 1 is Sunday night in Milwaukee. The Dodgers listed 13 pitchers on their NLCS roster. Infielder Hyeseong Kim was left off the Dodgers' NLCS roster after being included for the NL Division Series. The utility man posted a .259/.323/.328 batting line in 43 games this season. He appeared in one game in the NLDS as a defensive replacement. --Field Level Media

item.title: Lazio keep pace at the top, Juve, Milan and Roma all held
item.description: Lazio maintained their impressive start to the season with a 3-1 win over Monza on Sunday to move level on points with Serie A leaders Inter Milan, while Juventus rescued a 1-1 draw at high-flying Cagliari.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lazio maintained their impressive start to the season with a 3-1 win over Monza on Sunday to move level on points with Serie A leaders Inter Milan, while Juventus rescued a 1-1 draw at high-flying Cagliari. Ten-man AS Roma held on to draw 0-0 at Como and AC Milan were pegged back in a 1-1 draw at Sassuolo. Inter moved to 16 points with Saturday's [USN:L6N45W06R TEXT:"3-0 win over Parma"] and Lazio joined them despite almost allowing 10-man Monza back in the game. Roma are two points behind in third, with Cagliari fourth on 13 points and Milan a further point back in fifth spot. Juventus and Como are on 11 points. Gennaro Gattuso's Lazio took a third-minute lead at the Stadio Olimpico when Nuno Tavares rifled an unstoppable shot into the roof of the net. Midway through the first half, Lazio doubled their advantage with Gustav Isaksen finding the far bottom corner with a first-time shot from wide in the box. Monza's comeback chances then took a hammering when they had Lorenzo Lucchesi sent off 10 minutes before the break. Instead, Lazio appeared to switch off, and Monza pulled one back in the opening minute of the second half. Dany Mota flicked on a corner for Saba Goglichidze to head home, and for long periods the visitors had Lazio under the cosh. Mota was twice denied by Lazio keeper Christos Mandas before Lazio regrouped and finished off Monza's challenge two minutes from time through Andrea Pinamonti's strike from the edge of the six-yard box. "We can't afford to play like we did in the second half," Gattuso told DAZN. "We shouldn't be trying to manage the game. We need to keep doing things the right way." ROMA AND MILAN LOSE GROUND Roma were without injured keeper Mile Svilar, allowing Pierluigi Gollini to make his first league appearance since joining the club in January 2025. Gollini was in action early on, denying Nico Paz's attempted chip and at the other end Lorenzo Pellegrini's shot hit the upright in an evenly contested opening half. It was mostly one-way traffic, however, once Roma's Donyell Malen was sent off eight minutes after the break and Como piled on the pressure in search of a winner. Tasos Douvikas fired a shot into the side netting, and Gollini again saved from Paz as Roma hung on to earn a point in the first scoreless draw of the season in Serie A. Milan also lost ground on the leaders after surrendering a second-half advantage at Sassuolo, although they remain unbeaten this season. Sassuolo keeper Arijanet Muric made saves from Goncalo Ramos, Diego Moreira and Strahinja Pavlovic to keep the game goalless at the break. Milan introduced Luka Modric from the bench at the start of the second half, and the Croatian playmaker set up the opening goal in the 63rd minute with a pass into Adrien Rabiot, who scored from a tight angle. Sassuolo levelled five minutes later, Cas Odenthal firing past Mike Maignan through a crowded six-yard box following a corner kick. Cagliari, who had won four of their opening five matches, appeared on course for another victory after Daniel Maldini gave them a 20th-minute lead against Juventus. The visitors rescued a draw nine minutes from time when substitute Kerim Alajbegovic crossed to the back post for Randal Kolo Muani to score his first league goal of the season. Juventus manager Luciano Spalletti and his Cagliari counterpart Fabio Pisacane were both shown red cards following a verbal altercation after the final whistle.

item.title: EUA ameaçam bloquear armas para Ucrânia devido a ataques a refinarias, diz FT
item.description: Os EUA estão ameaçando suspender o sistema de aquisição que fornece armas à Ucrânia, a fim de pressionar Kiev a interromper seus ataques contra a infraestrutura energética russa, informou o Financial Times no domingo, citando autoridades europeias.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os EUA estão ameaçando suspender o sistema de aquisição que fornece armas à Ucrânia, a fim de pressionar Kiev a interromper seus ataques contra a infraestrutura energética russa, informou o Financial Times no domingo, citando autoridades europeias. As autoridades, que receberam ligações de autoridades norte-americanas ou foram informadas sobre o assunto, afirmaram que os EUA estavam pressionando as capitais europeias e Kiev para tentar pôr fim aos ataques às refinarias de petróleo russas, acrescentou a reportagem. A Reuters não conseguiu verificar a notícia imediatamente. A Casa Branca não respondeu de imediato a um pedido de comentário. A mensagem dos EUA incluía ameaças de interromper o compartilhamento de inteligência e o mecanismo Purl (Lista de Necessidades Prioritárias da Ucrânia) para a aquisição de armas norte-americanas pela Ucrânia, acrescentou a reportagem. “Eles estão ligando para Kiev... Estão ligando para todo mundo [na Europa]”, disse uma autoridade que recebeu uma ligação de um representante do Ministério da Defesa dos EUA, segundo a reportagem. A reportagem surge depois que o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, fez um anúncio surpresa no domingo sobre um cessar-fogo energético entre a Rússia e a Ucrânia que, segundo ele, entraria “em vigor imediatamente”, mas o líder ucraniano Volodymyr Zelenskiy afirmou que ainda estava aguardando os detalhes do acordo.

item.title: Ukraine awaits details of ceasefire proposals from US, Russia maintains attacks, Zelenskiy says
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said he was waiting for the details of an energy ceasefire with Russia announced by US President Donald Trump on Sunday, but that Ukraine supported such an agreement.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said he was waiting for the details of an energy ceasefire with Russia announced by US President Donald Trump on Sunday, but that Ukraine supported such an agreement. Zelenskiy also said that Russian forces were maintaining their attacks on Ukrainian energy targets regardless of Trump's announcement. "Ukraine supports the ceasefire, and it is important that Russia support it as well. We are awaiting details from the American side," Zelenskiy said in a post on the Telegram app. He noted that he had discussed Trump's announcement with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Finnish President Alex Stubb. "For our part, Ukraine always FULLY supports steps toward de-escalation, the protection of lives, and the decisions needed to end the war and guarantee lasting peace," Zelenskiy said. Speaking later in his nightly video address, Zelenskiy said Russian forces were still launching air attacks on energy infrastructure, including a strike on a joint heating and power plant in Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city. "Right now, there are Shaheds in the sky," he said, referring to Iranian-designed drones. "And there were strikes, unfortunately, with aerial bombs. There were strikes on our energy infrastructure. Just now, there was a strike on the joint power and heating plant in the city of Kharkiv – hitting Kharkiv's energy system." Zelenskiy said there had been more than 200 strikes on Ukrainian generating capacity in the past week and 17 on oil and gas installations.
